regulation: Food Safety and Standards (Alcoholic Beverages) Regulations, 2018

official_sources.title: Food Safety and Standards (Alcoholic Beverages) Regulations, 2018 — Compendium Version V (04.12.2025)

current_effective_notes: Version V includes final June 2025 provisions effective 1 January 2026. The 27 November 2025 direction extends labelling provisions to 1 July 2026; it is not treated here as a blanket composition extension.
RTD definition says more than 0.5% and up to 15%, while amended Table 4 says below 15%. Exactly 15% is blocked for source reconciliation, not approved through the definition alone.
Alcohol-free beer is defined at 0.0% abv and otherwise follows the regular-beer parameters.
Craft beer and flavoured beer provisions are included; current craft-beer Table-3 notes cover CO2/N2 mixtures and microbiological treatment.
The final November 2025 Table 2 fruit-wine ester amendment is effective 1 June 2026. The January 2026 corrigendum changes the place of notification only.

general_requirements.scope: Distilled and un-distilled alcoholic beverages regulated under the Alcoholic Beverages Regulations.
general_requirements.product_rule: Ethanol used in alcoholic beverages shall be of agricultural origin.
general_requirements.additives_rule: Food additives and flavours are allowed only where permitted under applicable FSSAI regulations and the mapped Appendix A FCS. The PMSV uploaded Appendix A Version 3 dataset remains the additive-permission layer.
general_requirements.test_methods: Use the current FSSAI Manual of Methods of Analysis of Foods — Alcoholic Beverages, as amended from time to time.
general_requirements.bulk_container_label: Bulk containers shall carry the declaration 'For Manufacturer of Alcoholic Beverages only'.
general_requirements.microbiology_general: Where the product standard specifies absence/limits, apply those product-specific requirements.

2.1.name: Brandy
2.1.definition_summary: Alcoholic beverage made by distillation of wine; current regulation provides grape, blended and Indian-brandy routes.
current_label_notes: For fruit brandy other than grape, prefix the fruit name to 'Brandy'.
Indian Brandy carries the prescribed source-spirit statement and name-format requirements.
source_questions_r11: Indian brandy is defined but has no separately labelled Table 1 column; do not select grape/blended limits by name alone.

2.2.name: Country liquors or Indian Liquors
variants: Plain country liquor / Plain Indian liquor
Blended country liquor / Blended Indian liquor
2.2.definition_summary: Distilled alcoholic beverages from fermentable carbohydrates of agricultural origin; Annexure-1 lists product names and raw materials non-exhaustively.

2.3.name: Fenny or Feni
2.3.definition_summary: Distilled liquor made from fermented cashew-apple juice or coconut toddy.

2.4.name: Gin
2.4.definition_summary: Distilled alcoholic beverage made from neutral spirit of agricultural origin and flavoured with juniper berries and/or other botanical flavouring agents.

2.5.name: Rum
2.5.definition_summary: Alcoholic distillate from fermented sugarcane juice, molasses or other sugarcane product; colouring other than caramel is not permitted. White rum is uncoloured.

2.6.name: Vodka
2.6.definition_summary: Distilled alcoholic beverage made from neutral spirit obtained from fermented agricultural carbohydrate sources.

2.7.name: Liqueur or Cordial or Aperitif
2.7.definition_summary: Distilled-spirit beverage flavoured with fruit, cream, herbs, spices, essential oils or botanical products; may contain more than 2.5% sugars/sweeteners as specified.

2.8.name: Whisky or Whiskey
2.8.definition_summary: Alcoholic beverage made by distilling fermented cereal-grain extract and/or using permitted grain/neutral/rectified agricultural spirits under the current definitions.

2.9.name: Pot-still distilled spirit
2.9.definition_summary: Alcoholic beverage obtained by pot-still distillation from permitted fermented agricultural carbohydrate sources; colouring is restricted to caramel/natural ageing-derived colour under the standard.
source_questions_r11: Catalogue groups pot and column distillation, but clause 2.9/Table 1 identifies pot-distilled spirit. Column-only mapping remains unresolved.

3.1.1.1.name: Red wine
3.1.1.1.definition_summary: Wine from red grapes or a mixture of red and white grapes fermented with skin contact; rosé follows the red-wine requirements.

3.1.1.2.name: White wine
3.1.1.2.definition_summary: Wine prepared from white grapes or juice extracted after removal of red-grape skins.

3.1.2.1.name: Semi sparkling or Crackling wine
3.1.2.1.definition_summary: Wine with carbon dioxide 3.0–5.0 g/L or 1.5–2.5 bar at 20°C resulting from primary or secondary fermentation.

3.1.2.2.name: Sparkling wine
3.1.2.2.definition_summary: Wine with carbon dioxide minimum 7.0 g/L or 3.5 bar at 20°C from primary or secondary fermentation.

sugar_classes.name: Extra-Dry
sugar_classes.rule: more than 1.2% up to 1.7% sugar, tolerance 0.3%

sugar_classes.name: Dry
sugar_classes.rule: more than 1.7% up to 3.2% sugar, tolerance 0.3%

3.1.2.3.name: Carbonated wine
3.1.2.3.definition_summary: Wine made effervescent with carbon dioxide other than that resulting solely from secondary fermentation.

3.1.4.name: Wine from fruits other than grapes
3.1.4.definition_summary: Wine produced by normal alcoholic fermentation of fruit other than grapes; fruit name is prefixed to wine.

3.1.4.4.name: Honey wine or Mead
3.1.4.4.definition_summary: Wine from fermentation of an aqueous solution of honey by yeasts without another carbohydrate source; herbs, spices or natural flavourings may be used.
3.1.4.4.current_effective_note: Mead composition insertion is in the final first amendment effective 1 January 2026. The 27 November 2025 direction specifically extends labelling compliance to 1 July 2026; source-scope distinction retained.
3.1.4.4.ester_limit_reference_r11: The Table 2 fruit-wine column including honey wine: 3.0 g/L absolute alcohol from 1 June 2026; do not transfer to cider, perry or other-plant-wine columns.

3.1.5.1.name: Palm wine/Toddy
3.1.5.1.definition_summary: Wine prepared from sap of palm trees and coconut palms.

3.1.6.name: Wine Based Beverages
3.1.6.table_basis: Table 2 table-wine requirements except ethyl alcohol content, as amended. Actual base-wine category must be established.
3.1.6.definition_summary: Wine-based beverage with the printed at least 50 by volume wine wording, permitted treatments and additions. The missing percentage symbol/denominator is retained as a source question, not silently repaired.
3.1.6.current_note: May or may not be carbonated under the current Version V amendment.
source_questions_r11: Printed wine-fraction wording needs original-source unit reconciliation. Do not automatically invoke the wine-specific expiry exemption for a wine-based beverage without establishing scope.

4.1.name: Beer
quality_rules: Clear except wheat beer, with characteristic colour/taste/bouquet.
Bottled/canned beer is pasteurized or filter sterilized; draught beer may or may not be.
Free from coliforms and other pathogenic microorganisms.
source_questions_r11: Table 3 carbonation heading says Min while cells print 1.8-3.6. Source interpretation is required before automatic range acceptance. CO2/N2 mixture permission is craft-specific.

4.2.name: Draught Beer
current_rules: Craft beer may be aromatized with suitable food ingredients and may or may not be filtered/pasteurized.
Flavoured beer uses flavours permitted under the Food Products Standards and Food Additives Regulations and must meet the other beer requirements.
Nitro Craft Beer uses a mixture of CO2 and N2 gas under the current provision.
source_questions_r11: Table 3 carbonation heading says Min while cells print 1.8-3.6. Source interpretation is required before automatic range acceptance. CO2/N2 mixture permission is craft-specific.

1.2.4a/1.3.9.name: Alcoholic Ready-to-Drink Beverages
1.2.4a/1.3.9.definition_summary: Flavoured beverage made from spirit/mixture of spirit or other alcoholic beverage base with permitted flavours/additives and optional fruit/vegetable juice, herbs, spices, sugar/caloric sweeteners, salt and carbonation. The amended definition uses up to 15%, unlike the strict upper bound in Table 4.
1.2.4a/1.3.9.carbonation_rule: Carbonated RTD beverages use carbon dioxide with minimum one volume and must conform to Table 4.

shared_wine_rules: Wine shall be clear with characteristic colour, taste, bouquet and form of its type.
Wine shall be preserved by pasteurization or permitted preservatives and be free from coliforms and pathogenic microorganisms.

Water added in preparation of wine shall not exceed 70 ml per kg of grape or fruit for the purposes permitted in the current regulation; dilution of high-sugar must shall not reduce it below 13.5°Brix.
Wine may be ameliorated using dry sugar or jaggery, separately or in combination, not more than 20%, as specified.

alcohol_specific_labelling: Declare alcohol content as % abv or proof.
Pot-distilled alcohol shall carry the prescribed pot-still / pot-distilled wording.
A standard drink is defined as the amount containing 12.7 ml alcohol by volume; approximate number of standard drinks may be stated.
Apply the current statutory warning required by the Alcoholic Beverages Regulations; size requirements depend on pack size.
Additional product-specific naming and declarations apply where stated in the individual standard.
final_compliance_lock: Do not issue a full alcoholic-product formulation verdict until the exact applicable Table 1/2/3 matrix row and all linked Appendix A, contaminants, microbiology, processing aids and current labelling rules are machine-validated.

source_review_r11.scope: Selected core source findings only. The full variant/row registry and comparator are offline companions and not wired into the live engine.
